[NDET.2.4] **`libds.h` names its release at compile time.** It must define
four macros, each naming the release the header belongs to:

| Macro | Value |
|---|---|
| `DS_VERSION_MAJOR` | the release's major number, a decimal integer literal |
| `DS_VERSION_MINOR` | its minor number, a decimal integer literal |
| `DS_VERSION_PATCH` | its patch number, a decimal integer literal |
| `DS_VERSION_STRING` | a string literal: the three numbers, in that order, joined by `.` |

The three numbers are usable in a preprocessor `#if`, so one source tree can
build against two releases. The version is the DS version of [LDET.1.10] in its
clean form: three numbers and nothing else, with no pre-release or build suffix.
The macros are written when a release is cut, and never by hand.

**The run-time version extends the compile-time one.** For a libds a release
ships, the `libds_version` that `ds_engine_get_platform_signature` reports, and
the `ds_version` a recording's header carries ([LFST.4.3]), must begin with
`DS_VERSION_STRING` followed by `+`. What follows the `+` names the build and is
provenance only. So a header and a library from one release agree on the
`<major>.<minor>.` prefix [LDET.1.10] compares.
